messages:
li (pm): Quick thread: proposing a different angle for Dedicated roadmap - focus on tenant-controlled grace windows + dynamic quota slabs to reduce firing of preemptive drains. Need acceptance criteria and pilot plan.

devin (sre): sounds good. grace windows were requested by a couple customers. curious how "dynamic quota slabs" differs from soft caps we already have.

li (pm): idea: instead of a single fixed reserved headroom per tier, we maintain multiple slabs that customers can opt into per workload. slabs = (baseline, launch, batch) with configurable % headroom and duration. system can auto-promote slab during detected launches or when customer schedules a window.

tara (prod-eng): +1. operationally we can implement slabs as time-limited admission-control overrides and a short-lived token bucket reservation. Example API below.

sam (acct mgr): customers will want visibility and billing clarity. if we reserve tokens in a slab, does that mean they pay for reserved capacity even when unused? need clear optional billing.

mika (legal): also need contract language for scheduled windows and opt-in billing. if a customer triggers an emergency slab we should capture consent in audit logs.

infra-bot: perf-check: remember earlier experiment where 10% reserved headroom caused fillstarvation in bronze pools. see logs/2025-01-14.

li (pm): proposed concrete:
- slabs: baseline (0% reserve), launch (10-20% reserve), batch (5% reserved)
- slabs are per-pool and per-tenant, configurable via API and UI
- scheduled grace windows: customer schedules start/duration, system sets slab to launch for that window
- auto-detect: heuristics detect >=2x baseline sustained qps for 5m -> auto-suggest launch slab to tenant (requires opt-in)

API sketch:
```
POST /v1/dedicated/pools/:pool_id/slabs
{ "name": "launch", "reserve_pct": 15, "duration_mins": 120, "billing_option": "reserve-if-used" }
PUT /v1/dedicated/pools/:pool_id/grace-windows
{ "start": "2025-07-10T17:00Z", "duration_mins": 30, "slab": "launch" }
GET /v1/dedicated/pools/:pool_id/usage?window=1h
```

devin (sre): technical constraints: token-bucket reservation requires fast path in admission controller and a reconciliation loop to free unused reservations after window expiry. need telemetry: reserved_tokens, used_tokens, reservation_wastage.

tara (prod-eng): autoscale interaction: if slab reserve is active we should lower aggressive autoscale triggers (avoid spinning extra GPUs unless actual consumption). also need preemption policy when multiple tenants ask for launch slabs simultaneously on constrained pools.

sam (acct mgr): billing options proposed: "reserve-paid" (pay for reserved capacity whether used), "reserve-if-used" (pay only for used tokens within slab), and "no-billing" for trial pilot. which do we want for pilot?

li (pm): pilot plan: offer to 3 customers as opt-in with "reserve-if-used" billing and manual SLA note. Pilot duration 3 weeks. Acceptance: no more than 2% tail SLA violations for gold during pilot; slab activation/expiry are correct 99% of times.

mika (legal): will draft short pilot addendum. need audit trail retention 90 days for scheduled windows and manual-trigger events.

devin (sre): rollout stages suggestion:
M1 (2 sprints): admission-controller changes to support slabs + telemetry metrics emitted (reserved_tokens, used_tokens, wasted_pct), API endpoints (read-only).
M2 (3 sprints): enable scheduling, opt-in auto-detect, bill mode support for "reserve-if-used", UI toggles for tenants. add reconciliation background worker.
M3 (2 sprints): conflict resolution for simultaneous slabs, fairness algorithm, rollout to more pools + extended pilot.

li (pm): risks:
- wasted reserved capacity (cost) if customers set high slabs then don't use them.
- complexity in fairness when many tenants request slabs at once.
- legal/billing edge cases for refunds.

tara (prod-eng): mitigation: add 'waste cap' alerts (e.g., wasted_pct > 30% over 24h) and auto-revoke slabs for trial accounts. also surface tenant recommendations after pilot.

sam (acct mgr): i'll collect pilot candidates and filter for tenants who run scheduled launches (marketing, product release cycles). want a short FAQ for customers on how slab billing works.

mika (legal): I'll prepare the pilot addendum draft and sample audit log schema.

li (pm): acceptance criteria (short list):
- API to create/delete slabs and schedule grace windows exists and is stable
- admission controller respects active slab reservations under load in staging e2e (chaos test pass)
- telemetry: reserved_tokens, used_tokens, wasted_pct, slab_activations emitted to console and billing exports
- pilot run with 3 customers for 3 weeks; SLA metrics meet thresholds; pilot addendum signed

devin (sre): ops tasks: runbook for slab revocation, dashboard panels for slab utilization, and an hourly synthetic that activates a slab and verifies admission behavior.

li (pm): prioritization: recommend we treat this as adjacent-path to preemptive drain work. M1 gets highest priority because we need admission changes before we can do drains safely.

tara (prod-eng): agree. I'll slot M1 in next sprint and start design doc this afternoon.

li (pm): thanks all. sync Friday 10am for pilot candidate review. please drop any missing acceptance items here. :rocket:
